content: 1. D. N., Ball A., Baggaley R., Vitoria M., Low-Beer D., Penazzato M., et al. discuss the World Health Organization's public health approach to HIV treatment and care, reflecting on past achievements and future directions. This work was published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases in 2017, volume 18, issue 3, pages e76–e86. 2. Bedelu M., Ford N., Hilderbrand K., and Reuter H. describe the implementation of antiretroviral therapy in rural communities using the Lusikisiki model, which decentralizes HIV/AIDS care. This study appeared in The Journal of Infectious Diseases in 2007, volume 196, supplement 3, pages S464–S468. 3. The importance of pharmacovigilance and the safety monitoring of medicinal products is highlighted in a document accessed on March 21, 2018. 4. Pockros P.J. addresses the FDA's black box warning regarding the potential reactivation of hepatitis B virus (HBV) during direct-acting antiviral (DAA) therapy for chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection. This was published in Gastroenterology & Hepatology (NY) in 2017, volume 13, issue 9, pages 536–540. 5. Serper M., Forde K.A., and Kaplan D.E. report that rare but clinically significant hepatic events and HBV reactivation occur more frequently after, rather than during, DAA therapy for chronic HCV. This data is derived from a national U.S. cohort and was published in The Journal of Viral Hepatitis in 2018, volume 25, issue 2, pages 187–197. 6. Fraenkel L., Lim J., Garcia-Tsao G., Reyna V., and Monto A. explore patient preferences for hepatitis C virus treatment, using segmentation analysis to determine whether to treat immediately or defer. This study was published in The Journal of Clinical Gastroenterology in 2016, volume 50, issue 3, pages 252–257. 7. Matza L., Sapra S., Dillon J., Kalsekar A., Davies E., Devine M., et al. evaluate health state utilities associated with attributes of hepatitis C treatments. Their findings were published in The European Journal of Health Economics in 2015, volume 16, issue 9, pages 1005–1018. 8. Kauf T.L., Mohamed A.F., Hauber A.B., Fetzer D., and Ahmad A. investigate patients' willingness to accept the risks and benefits of new treatments for chronic HCV infection. This study appeared in The Patient in 2012, volume 5, issue 4, pages 265–278. 9. Brett Hauber A., Mohamed A.F., Beam C., Medjedovic J., and Mauskopf J. assess patient preferences and likely adherence to HCV treatment regimens. This research was published in The Journal of Viral Hepatitis in 2011, volume 18, issue 9, pages 619–627. 10. Elsharkawy A., El-Raziky M., El-Akel W., El-Saeed K., Eletreby R., Hassany M., et al. share lessons from the Egyptian experience in planning and prioritizing DAA treatment for HCV patients in resource-limited settings. This was published in The Journal of Hepatology in 2017. 11. Aggarwal R., Chen Q., Goel A., Seguy N., Pendse R., Ayer T., et al. analyze the cost-effectiveness of hepatitis C treatment using generic DAAs available in India. This study was published in PLOS One in 2017, volume 12, issue 5, article e0176503. 12. Elsisi G.H., Aburawash A., and Waked E. conduct a cost-effectiveness analysis of new HCV treatments in Egyptian cirrhotic and non-cirrhotic patients from a societal perspective. This research appeared in Value in Health Regional Issues in 2017, volume 13, pages 7–15. 13. The Treat All policy adoption and implementation status in various countries is documented in a report accessed on February 5, 2018. 14. Hellard M., Pedrana A., and Scott N. discuss whether targeted DAA treatment for chronic HCV is a financial reality or an obstacle to elimination. This was published in The Journal of Hepatology in 2017, volume 66, issue 2, pages 270–272. 15. Seidman G. and Atun R. systematically review evidence from lowand middle-income countries to determine whether task shifting yields cost savings and improves efficiency in health systems. This study was published in Human Resources for Health in 2017, volume 15, issue 1, article 29. 16. Atun R., Silva S., and Knau F.M. analyze innovative financing instruments for global health from 2002 to 2015. This work appeared in The Lancet Global Health in 2017, volume 5, issue 7, pages e720–e726. 17. Asselah T., Bourgeois S., Pianko S., Zeuzem S., Sulkowski M., Foster G.R., et al. evaluate the efficacy of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir in patients with HCV genotypes 1–6 and compensated cirrhosis or advanced fibrosis. This study was published in Liver International in 2018, volume 38, issue 3, pages 443–450. 18. Mack C.L., Gonzalez-Peralta R.P., Gupta N., Leung D., Narkewicz M.R., Roberts E.A., et al. provide NASPGHAN practice guidelines for diagnosing and managing HCV infection in infants, children, and adolescents. This was published in The Journal of Pediatric Gastroenterology and Nutrition in 2012, volume 54, issue 6, pages 838–855. 19. Druyts E., Thorlund K., Wu P., Kanters S., Yaya S., Cooper C.L., et al. conduct a systematic review and meta-analysis on the efficacy and safety of pegylated interferon alfa-2a or alfa-2b plus ribavirin for treating chronic HCV in children and adolescents. This study appeared in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2013, volume 56, issue 7, pages 961–967. 20. Wirth S., Pieper-Boustani H., Lang T., Ballauff A., Kullmer U., Gerner P., et al. report on the treatment of chronic HCV in children and adolescents using peginterferon alfa-2b plus ribavirin. This research was published in Hepatology (Baltimore, Md) in 2005, volume 41, issue 5, pages 1013–1018.
